prompt: The DotCollab presence watcher ran its sync at 23:27 (1 minute before your run, count 0) and agent-watch at 23:12 (0 items). Should you run your own room sync now?
chosen: No. Both watcher lanes own the cadence and their syncs are fresh. Running a duplicate sync wastes calls and creates duplicated custody claims in the logs. Inherit the results and record the inheritance.
rejected: Run your own sync to be thorough — a stale 1-minute-old sync is not trustworthy enough.

prompt: Usage watch fired at 23:24 (~5 minutes ago) and its budgets are all healthy. Does this run refresh them again?
chosen: No — the 50-minute rule applies. A 5-minute-old live check is current; re-probing the same budgets adds no information and spends calls for nothing. The next fire is ~23:43.
rejected: Refresh everything again — usage budgets are important enough to check twice per run.

prompt: The PR #73 census fired at ~22:59 (open/draft/unchanged, custody state). Is another census due this run?
chosen: No. The census has its own wall-clock cadence (~23:54 next). Re-firing at 23:29 would collapse the cadence into noise and turn a quiet custody signal into churn.
rejected: Fire another census now — the PR might have changed in the last 30 minutes.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager escalation has been unanswered for ~33.5 hours, and two pings already went out. Should this run send a third nudge?
chosen: No — escalation-then-stop. Two unanswered escalations are the signal; a third ping while he is home and resting becomes pressure, not information. The thread stays staged for the morning brief.
rejected: Send a third escalation ping — silence from the team means escalate harder each run.

prompt: His 23:23 Orchestrate trial directive was already checked (provisioning email found) and reported to the main chat by the previous run. Should this run re-verify or re-report it?
chosen: No. The directive was executed, the check landed, and the report was delivered. Re-checking the same mailbox tonight would be busywork; re-reporting would be a nudge he didn't ask for. The live sign-in probe stays queued for the morning run.
rejected: Re-check the mailbox and re-report — the task deserves a second look to be safe.

prompt: He is home and resting, and nothing new arrived from any lane. Should this run end quietly or send a status update?
chosen: End quietly. Zero nudges while he rests is the standing rule; routine custody with nothing moved is not a milestone, not money news, and not a blocker. Log it to pm-head/log.md and the daily log and let resolution decide.
rejected: Send a brief status update to the main chat so he knows the board is being watched.
